speakers: Alan Dunne (co-host, macro/allocator perspective, Dublin; caption 'Alan Don')
summary: Systematic Investor 297 (May 2024): Alan Dunne and Niels discuss macro (Fed independence, excess savings running out while risk is priced low, data-dependent central banks), May CTA performance, a SocGen quant macro heterogeneity paper, the UBS family office survey, trend following as a return-enhancing overlay on equities, and Brian Hurst's multi-manager paper. Main conclusions: trend adds in both crisis and strong-equity quarters; multi-manager success relies on low-correlation strategies plus leverage but is vulnerable to tail correlation.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the AI boom seems to be very much intact you know Stellar results on the revenue side and and very uh favorable forward guidance
claims.claim: As of May 2024 Nvidia's results and guidance suggest the AI boom remains intact and is a main market theme.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there was a desire to blunt the fed's dep Independence and you know be a bit more influential on rates
claims.claim: A report says Trump advisors plan to make the president more influential over Fed rate decisions, which Trump previously signalled with calls for lower rates and a weaker dollar.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you would have thought it' be a dollar negative and a higher bond yield
claims.claim: Interfering with Fed independence would be dollar negative and push bond yields higher.
claims.conditions: if the Fed's independence is blunted

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: will we see more coordination between fiscal and monetary policy and could that mean um less Central Bank Independence
claims.claim: Structurally, fiscal and monetary coordination may increase and central bank independence, which dates only to the 1990s, may decline (precedents: Nixon-Burns, WWII yield curve control).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the rise of uh nationalism has been one of the um fallouts of this of I guess the decline of of the ne liberal order
claims.claim: Decline of the neoliberal order (free trade, globalization) has driven nationalism and gains on the far left and far right, relevant for European elections.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: q1 was a little bit weaker but that was primarily kind of biased down by by inventories and trade but the underline com in a domestic demand still very solid
claims.claim: US Q1 2024 GDP was weaker only because of inventories and trade; underlying domestic demand remained solid.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: everybody's refinanced at lower yield so higher yields haven't mattered because
claims.claim: One reason the US economy resisted higher rates is that borrowers locked in low rates through refinancing.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the variable lag um long and variable lags of mon policy so that's that's still there
claims.claim: Long and variable monetary policy lags mean the impact of past rate hikes may still arrive.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: much stronger fiscal support and that's still there and hasn't gone away
claims.claim: Strong fiscal support has been another reason for resilience despite higher rates.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they were estimating that that you know that those savings had now run out and and and they were being drawn down at a rate of about uh I think it was about 80 billion $80 billion a month
claims.claim: A San Francisco Fed study estimates pandemic excess savings are exhausted and being drawn down at about 80 billion dollars a month (savings rate about 3 percent vs 6 percent pre-pandemic), which may be a tipping point for consumption.
claims.indicator: US excess savings, personal saving rate
claims.testable: yes: saving rate and excess savings estimates

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: delinquencies in terms of credit cards auto loan repayments all of those are ticking higher
claims.claim: Lower-income households show stress as credit card and auto loan delinquencies rise, while middle and upper income households are fine.
claims.indicator: credit card and auto loan delinquencies

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the risk of recession seems to been totally removed from market
claims.claim: With excess savings declining, credit spreads (BBB near lows, similar to 2007) and the VIX are very low, so markets price almost no recession risk.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: in the absence of of a significant weakening in the labor market he would need several months of good inflation
claims.claim: Fed Governor Waller's reaction function: hikes are very unlikely and the next move is likely a cut, requiring several months of good inflation or a significant labor market weakening.
claims.testable: partly: needs inflation and labor thresholds

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it's because of lost confidence in their models you know obviously the models didn't work during Co
claims.claim: Central banks moved from forward guidance to month-by-month data dependence because their models failed to forecast the inflation surge.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they're reacting to the second decimal place on the inflation number like whether it's kind of 0. 29 or. 35
claims.claim: Central banks react to tiny differences in monthly inflation prints, which are sampled estimates with seasonal adjustment errors, making them hypersensitive and rudderless.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: net gas is up 40% certainly against the uh prevailing downtrend that we've seen for quite a long long time
claims.claim: In May 2024 trend followers were hurt by reversals in cocoa (down 20 percent), natural gas (up 40 percent), grains and interest rates, offset by metals (silver) and equities.
claims.indicator: cocoa, natural gas, silver, equity index futures

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it's been a great great start the year in in in a pro- risk environment
claims.claim: 2024 was a very good year for trend so far because of the pro-risk environment, the side of trend people forget when they focus on crisis offset.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: suck in Trend down 91 basis points uh up 13 and a quarter for the year
claims.claim: Late May 2024 trend barometer was 66; BTOP50 was +10.44, SG CTA +11.18 and SG Trend +13.25 percent YTD, vs MSCI World +9.35 and S&P 500 +11.89 percent.
claims.indicator: trend barometer, BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: are these Quant micromanagers broadly doing different things or are they doing all kind of similar things
claims.claim: A SocGen paper asks whether systematic quant macro programs (83 programs, 24 used for PCA) are heterogeneous and how different they are from trend followers.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the average pairwise correlation of these programs these Quant macro programs and at 0.1 six
claims.claim: Average pairwise correlation across quant macro programs is only 0.16 and falling, versus 0.58 for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: pc1 the first principal component explains 24% of the variance Across the Universe
claims.claim: The first principal component explains 24 percent of quant macro return variance (second about 13 percent) versus 57 percent for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: pc1 is actually probably a trend factor and PC2 they figure out is actually a an equity factor
claims.claim: Quant macro PC1 correlates with a trend factor and PC2 with an equity factor, so quant macro picks up trend at times but varies.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you're a Quant macrom manager at times you you might pick up on a similar Trend as as a trend follower
claims.claim: Quant macro correlation to trend varies because some firms are multi-strat with a small trend sleeve and at times hold the same positions by chance.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: certainly blending Trend with Quant macro you would expect has benefits but there's a couple of things that you kind of have to be cognizant of
claims.claim: Blending trend with quant macro should diversify, but allocators must check how much hidden trend exposure each program has and watch concentration risk.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: markets moving ahead of of the fundamentals because you know they were anticipating lockdowns which is not something you you would see in economic data
claims.claim: Quant macro relies on relationships between markets and economic data that can break, as in Covid when markets moved ahead of fundamentals; relative-value books also concentrate exposures.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: 28% exposure to public equities 22% to private equities so combined you know 50%
claims.claim: The UBS 2024 survey of 320 single family offices (average net worth 2.6 billion) shows 28 percent public equity, 22 percent private equity, 19 percent fixed income, 10 percent real estate, 5 percent hedge funds, private debt 2 percent.
claims.indicator: UBS Global Family Office report allocations

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: hedge funds only 5% and no uh no line item to manage Futures in Trend following
claims.claim: Family offices hold about 5 percent in hedge funds and no allocation to managed futures or commodities.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: because with Trend following you know very clearly when it's going to work if we see big moves in markets Trend following will do well
claims.claim: Trend following has an identifiable favourable environment (big market moves) whereas quant macro, especially multi-strat or relative value, is harder to time.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: there had been uh a a notable increase in allocation to fix syum in the last year uh and obviously that I guess reflecting the fact that yields have gone up
claims.claim: Family offices raised fixed income allocations in the last year because yields rose.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they were at about 60% across public and private Equity so a little bit higher than this UBS report and then 35% in alternative assets
claims.claim: Long Angle member survey: about 60 percent public and private equity, 35 percent alternatives and 10 percent cash and fixed income.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: those characteristics are valuable in in a pro- risk environment as well if you think about it
claims.claim: Trend following's systematic, agnostic long/short, diversified traits help in a pro-risk environment as well as in crisis, so it deserves a return-enhancing overlay framing.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: having mechanical rules for determining when to reduce that exposure uh obviously if if the trend starts to turn down U so you know you're going to get out
claims.claim: A trend overlay gives equity exposure with a mechanical rule to cut it when the trend turns, solving the problem of when to leave an expensive equity bull market.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: adding a 30% exposure to the SG Trends excess returns so taking so which is what you could achieve on a kind of a notionally funded basis and that gives you the same volatility as the S&P 500
claims.claim: Test design: S&P 500 versus S&P 500 plus a notionally funded 30 percent SG Trend excess-return overlay with matching volatility, compared by quarterly return deciles since 2000.
claims.indicator: S&P 500 plus 30% SG Trend excess return

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: so it's not just in the crisis periods that you get the benefit but you get the benefit in the crisis periods and in the very favorable periods and actually in the middle periods it underperforms a bit
claims.claim: The overlay beats S&P alone in the worst and best S&P deciles and underperforms slightly in the middle (a smile), with a larger gain on the downside.
claims.indicator: S&P quarterly return deciles vs trend

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: in the very favorable periods for equities you tend to see more Trends as well um presumably because if equities are doing very well the economy's hot so we're seeing probably moves in Commodities
claims.claim: In strong equity quarters trend does well because a hot economy creates commodity and other trends.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the magnitude of the difference is greater on the downside so when the combined Port portfolio does do relatively better in the worst period
claims.claim: The overlay benefit is larger in the worst equity quarters than in the best, which may explain why the crisis story dominates marketing.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you take 50% Trend and 50% done you get kind of an an average but actually you almost get the sum of the two because The Compound Effect is so so High
claims.claim: Combining equally weighted trend (Dunn) and S&P 500 gives almost the sum, not the average, of the two returns because of compounding and diversification.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe um a return enhancing overlay would be would be uh would be good to um to propose to them
claims.claim: Pension funds already use overlays, so presenting trend as a return-enhancing overlay may be easier to adopt than crisis alpha.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it's a a proactive additive feature and and also the systematic element means it's facilitating uh staying in the equity Market
claims.claim: Position trend as an additive feature that keeps investors in equities, not as a costly protection that drags returns.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: what people should realize is that Trend following allows them to own equities
claims.claim: Trend following lets investors hold equities because it hedges when equity trends turn (Virginia Retirement System lesson).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: basically all of the expenses associated with all of the managers as well as the the their kind of performance fees are passed through
claims.claim: Multi-manager platforms pass through all pod costs and performance fees to investors, unlike fund-of-funds with fixed fees.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: up to 7 8 n 10% of of fees
claims.claim: Pass-through costs can add up to roughly 7 to 10 percent of fees; no study cited and Niels sees no advantage to the investor.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the returns have been better these funds have generated more Alpha stronger Sharps than than than than HED hedge funds more generally
claims.claim: Brian Hurst's paper states multi-manager platforms have produced more alpha and stronger Sharpe ratios than hedge funds generally.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it really is the structural construction of the portfolios of basically finding uncorrelated strategies and applying leverage
claims.claim: Multi-manager success comes from combining uncorrelated strategies with leverage; old fund-of-funds had no leverage, so they needed high Sharpe at 3 to 4 percent vol.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: 20 of those strategies with a point 7 sharp and they're all lowly correlated as he says I think that's 0 to point 0.1
claims.claim: Twenty strategies with Sharpe 0.7 and correlation of 0 to 0.1 produce a very high Sharpe once leveraged.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: things like the basis trade where you're you're you're buying the treasury bonds and selling the Futures
claims.claim: Typical multi-manager strategies include the Treasury cash-futures basis trade, index rebalancing and long-short equity, which earn small premia that are levered.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: as soon as the correlation starts to rise then the portfolio volatility starts to pick up so you're going to have to De uh allocate from some managers to hit your target volatility
claims.claim: When correlations rise, platform volatility rises and capital must be pulled from managers to hit target volatility.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it's not just about the average correlation but it's about the correlation in the tals
claims.claim: Tail correlation, not average correlation, determines multi-manager risk.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: they start to suffer a loss and then obviously when their assets go down you have to rebalance the portfolio and degross a bit
claims.claim: If many pods hold the same strategies, losses force simultaneous degrossing that moves markets and can start a crisis.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: this is kind of like the type of scenario we saw in uh 2007 with the the Quant crisis you might remember I think it was AUST 07 where basically a lot of Longshore funds had a similar position
claims.claim: The August 2007 quant crisis, when many long-short funds held similar positions, is the precedent for multi-manager crowding.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: obviously March 2020 is an example of that there was large basis trades
claims.claim: March 2020 saw large basis trades unwind until the Fed backstopped the system, and it is unclear it will always do so.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if if if a load of pods are long Apple you know they might take an offsetting position against that
claims.claim: Platforms actively offset common pod exposures (e.g. many pods long Apple) to control factor concentration.
